newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't okays Patagonia power line project.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't okays Patagonia power line project.

text.p: The Argentine government's electricity watchdog Enre has approved plans for a $250 million investment to deliver electricity to Buenos Aires from Patagonia, generating company Capex said Friday
Capex said in a statement that the Fourth Line project would add an extra 1,300 megawatts to the capital's energy supplies, boosting capacity especially during peak hours.
"It will involve $250 million in investment and the creation of 3,000 jobs, directly and indirectly," said Capex.

Eight Argentine utility companies have forged a strategic alliance to build the power line from Patagonia's Comahue area, as well as a $25 million capacitor project to boost electrical supply to Buenos Aires and surrounding areas.
Because of laws barring generators from owning electricity transport services, the group of companies plans to call an international tender to build the power line.
Capex said the tender would take place on July 31 and "once approved it is estimated that commercial operations of the project would begin in 24 months."
